Compute the mean x and median m of the eight numbers \(1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11\) 15. Let \[f (x) = \sqrt{x}\].

Apply this transformation to the data, and then com- pute the mean \(x̃\) and the median \(m̃\) of the transformed data

question a: \[\text{ Is}\,\, f (x) = x̃?\] question b: \[\text{Is} f ( m ) = m̃?\]

#we write up the data 
x=c(1,2,4,5,6,8,11)
#calculate the transformed data
fx=sqrt(x)
# find the mean for the data
xb=mean(x)
#then the mean of the transformation 
mean(fx)
## [1] 2.177832
#then f of the mean 
sqrt(xb)
## [1] 2.299068
#now we do the exactly the same but for the median 
m=median(x)
median(fx)
## [1] 2.236068
sqrt(m)
## [1] 2.236068

the mean is not equal since f is concave then
\[f(\dfrac{1}{n}*\sum_{i=1}^nx_i)\leq \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^nf(x_i)\] the median in this case is equal but this is only true in general when f in linear or n is uneven and f is montone

Let x and m denote the mean and median, respectively, of \[x_1 < x_2 < · · · < x_n\] Let f be a real-valued function.

  1. Is f(x) the mean off \[f(x_1),f(x_2),...,f(x_n)\]? no simply look at the last exercise

  2. Is f(m) the median off f(x1),f(x2),…,f(xn)? try \(x=(x_1,x_2)=(1,2)\) \(f=x^2\) not equal

  3. Are there any conditions that would ensure that f (x) is the mean of the transformed data? liniarity of f or no variance in x

  4. Are there any conditions that would ensure that f (m) is the median of the transformed data?

liniarity of f or no variance in x or f order preserving and n uneven

oms opgave 1.25 part a)

\[\hat{F}_n(x)=\dfrac{1}{n}*\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{1}_{]-\infty,x]}(X_i)\]

vi noterer at: \[\mathbb{1}_{]-\infty,x]}(X_i)=1\Leftrightarrow X_i\leq x\] og \[\mathbb{1}_{]-\infty,x]}(X_i)=0\Leftrightarrow X_i> x\] da er denne transformation bernulli med sandylingheds paramete \[\mathbb{P}(X_i \leq x)=F(x)\] summen af i.i.d bernulli er binomial \[n*\hat{F}_n(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{1}_{]-\infty,x]}(X_i)\] er da binomial

del b)

\[\mathbb{E}[\hat{F}_n(x)]=\dfrac{1}{n}*\mathbb{E}[n*\hat{F}_n(x)]=F(x)\]

\[\mathbb{V}[\hat{F}_n(x)]=\dfrac{1}{n^2}*\mathbb{V}[n*\hat{F}_n(x)]=\dfrac{1}{n^2}*n*F(x)*[1-F(x)]\]

\[=\dfrac{1}{n}*F(x)*(1-F(x))\]

del c) vis

\[\lim_{n\to \infty}\mathbb{P}(\lvert \hat{F}_n(x)-F(x)\lvert \geq \delta)=0 \quad \forall \delta>0\]

vi bemærker at \[\hat{F}_n(x)=\dfrac{1}{n}*\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{1}_{]-\infty,x]}(X_i)\] er en stikprøvemiddelværdi for varablen vi allerede har beskrevet som bernulli da siger store tals lov \[ \overline X \to^{\mathbb{P}} \mu \quad for\,\, n\to\infty \]

da \[\hat{F}_n(x)\] er en stkprøve middelværdi for bernulli må: \[\hat{F}_n(x) \to^{\mathbb{P}}F(x) \quad for\,\, n\to\infty \]
